dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the provenance correction report and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The lobby-facing hot desks review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I prepared the provenance correction for the Bemba mask in a reading-room carrel and sent it without a citation error.
Why did that setting work?
I could compare the accession ledgers without being pulled into visitor requests.
Someone new shadowed me in the Monday repatriation review this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the reading-room carrel into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
Last month I used a carrel to rebuild a donor file from three ledgers and the review panel accepted the report on first read.
Was the report ready on time?
Yes, because the source comparisons stayed uninterrupted.
I greet researchers at the lobby desk comfortably during their scheduled appointments.
Does public-facing work suit you?
It does when I am not reconstructing a chain of ownership.
I archived last cycle's notes on the lobby-facing hot desks and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
A carrel is open from 08:30 until the 11:30 repatriation review, and the lobby shift begins at noon.
Can both commitments fit?
Yes, the drafting can be complete before I take the desk.
A vendor call about the provenance correction report ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the Monday repatriation review checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the reading-room carrel.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the lobby-facing hot desks records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
At the lobby desk during the Maroon collection review, two visitor requests pulled me away from a ledger comparison and I carried an unchecked accession number into the draft.
Was the error caught?
Yes, but only during the final review.
I sketched next week's plan for the reading-room carrel before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the provenance correction report updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The panel chair has confirmed that no new collection material will arrive before the 11:30 review.
Does that limit last-minute research?
Yes, the carrel session can be used to finish the existing record.
I compared two options for the lobby-facing hot desks tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the Monday repatriation review handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The visitor-services lead asks whether I can take the lobby-facing hot desk Monday while the provenance correction report goes to review. How will I react?
